props.gloss_en: R' Yehoshua in the mishnah: one mentions rain from the last festival day of the festival
R' Yehoshua in the baraita: from the time the lulav is put down
R' Yehuda ben Beteira: on the second day of the festival he mentions
R' Yehuda in R' Yehoshua's name: of those passing before the ark on the last festival day of the festival, the last mentions [rain], the first does not
R' Yehuda in ben Beteira's name: of those passing before the ark on the last festival day of the festival, the last mentions
candidate: the R' Yehoshua R' Yehuda cites is the R' Yehoshua of the mishnah
candidate: he is the R' Yehoshua of the baraita
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: the R' Yehoshua R' Yehuda cites is R' Yehoshua ben Beteira
candidate: the ben Beteira R' Yehuda cites is R' Yehuda ben Beteira
Rav Nachman bar Yitzchak: the ben Beteira R' Yehuda cites is R' Yehoshua ben Beteira
sometimes [R' Yehuda] calls him by his own name, and sometimes by his father's name
this [citation] is from before he was ordained, and this from after he was ordained
dew and winds: the Sages did not obligate mentioning them, and if one comes to mention them, he mentions
R' Chanina: [mentioning them is optional] because they are not withheld
dew is not withheld
winds are not withheld

dew's not being withheld is derived from 'go show yourself to Ahab and I will give rain' (I Kings 18:1), set beside Elijah's oath of 'no dew or rain' (I Kings 17:1): God promised rain and did not mention dew -- because dew is not withheld
this is what Elijah said: even the dew of blessing will not come
[God did not restore the dew of blessing explicitly] because the matter is not recognisable
R' Yehoshua ben Levi: winds' not being withheld is derived from 'for as the four winds of the heavens have I spread you, says the Lord' (Zech 2:10)
candidate reading: God says to Israel, I scattered you to the four winds of the world
the reading: just as the world cannot be without winds, so the world cannot be without Israel
in the summer, one who said 'He makes the wind blow' is not sent back
in the summer, one who said 'He makes the rain fall' is sent back
in the rainy season, one who did not say 'He makes the wind blow' is not sent back
in the rainy season, one who did not say 'He makes the rain fall' is sent back
moreover, even one who said 'He removes the wind and lifts the dew' is not sent back
clouds and winds: the Sages did not obligate mentioning them, and if one comes to mention them, he mentions
the stam: because [clouds and winds] are not withheld -- clouds are not withheld
'and He will close up the heavens' (Deut 11:17) means from clouds and from winds: rain is said separately in 'and there will be no rain'
the winds that are not withheld are the common wind; the uncommon wind may be withheld
clouds and winds are second to rain
Ulla (some say Rav Yehuda): [the baraita speaks of clouds and winds] that come after rain
Ulla (some say Rav Yehuda): 'the Lord will make the rain of your land powder and dust' (Deut 28:24) is the wind after rain
Rav Yehuda: wind after rain is like rain
Rav Yehuda: clouds after rain are like rain
Rav Yehuda: sun after rain is like two rains
the stam: [Rav Yehuda's dictum] excludes the evening glow and the sun between the clouds
Rava: snow is as good for the mountains as five rains for the land
Rava's verse: 'for He says to the snow, be on the earth; and the shower of rain, and the showers of His mighty rain' (Job 37:6)
Rava: snow is good for the mountains
Rava: strong rain is good for trees
Rava: gentle rain is good for fruit
Rava: drizzle benefits even a seed under a clod
the stam: 'urpila' is 'uru pilei' -- arise, furrows
Rava: a young Torah scholar is like a seed under a clod: once it sprouts, it sprouts
Rava: a young Torah scholar who flares up -- it is the Torah that inflames him
Rava's verse: 'is not My word like fire, says the Lord' (Jer 23:29)
Rav Ashi: any Torah scholar who is not hard as iron is not a Torah scholar
Rav Ashi's verse: 'and like a hammer that shatters rock' (Jer 23:29)
R' Abba to Rav Ashi: you learn it from there; we learn it from here -- 'a land whose stones are iron' (Deut 8:9)
R' Abba: do not read 'its stones' (avaneha) but 'its builders' (boneha)
Ravina: even so, a person must teach himself gentleness
Ravina's verse: 'and remove anger from your heart' (Kohelet 11:10)
R' Yonatan: three asked improperly; two were answered properly and one improperly: Eliezer servant of Abraham, Saul son of Kish, and Jephthah the Gileadite
Eliezer asked improperly: 'the maiden to whom I say, let down your pitcher' (Gen 24:14) -- she might even have been lame or blind
he was answered properly: Rebecca came to him
Saul asked improperly: 'the man who kills him, the king will enrich ... and give him his daughter' (I Sam 17:25) -- he might even have been a slave or a mamzer
he was answered properly: David came to him
Jephthah asked improperly: 'whatever comes out of the doors of my house' (Jud 11:31) -- it might even have been something impure
he was answered improperly: his daughter came to him
the stam: this is what the prophet said to Israel, 'is there no balm in Gilead, is there no physician there?' (Jer 8:22)
the stam: 'which I did not command' (Jer 19:5) -- this is the son of Mesha king of Moab
the verse for Mesha: 'he took his firstborn son who would reign after him and offered him as a burnt offering' (II Kings 3:27)
'nor did I speak' -- this is Jephthah
'nor did it come into My heart' -- this is Isaac son of Abraham
R' Berekhya: the Congregation of Israel too asked improperly: 'and He will come to us like the rain' (Hos 6:3)
and the Holy One answered her properly
God: you ask for something sometimes wanted and sometimes not; I will be to you something always wanted -- 'I will be as the dew to Israel' (Hos 14:6)
R' Berekhya: and again she asked improperly: 'set me as a seal upon Your heart, as a seal upon Your arm' (Song 8:6)
God: you ask for something sometimes seen and sometimes not; I will make for you something always seen -- 'behold, I have engraved you on the palms of My hands' (Isa 49:16)
